judgment.notes: M002 uses X=R with its Borel structure, μ=λ, f=c1_I and g=∑g_i; F002 supplies the inequality on I, and off I all indicators vanish. M001 uses K=N and f(i)=g_i; N is countable and BG005-BG009 verify Borel indicators and a.e. measurability. Neither source requires finite integrals. M003 is used twice, with (T,constant)=(I,c) and (J_i∩I,ρ_i^s); both sets are measurable and both constants are nonnegative. M005 at 0,1 yields λ(I)=1. M006 applies to the real endpoints supplied by F001; their difference is positive and at most ρ_i+η_i. Empty intervals contribute zero as checked in BG013. No E applications occur.

S001's Euclidean distance comparison bounds both projected diameters; bounded nonempty real projections admit the explicit enclosing intervals, and the positive η_i gives containment even at infimum/supremum endpoints (BG001-BG003,BG014). Empty V_i uses J_i=∅. For each fixed t∈I, S002 truly obtains a δ-cover of E from active A_i; infimum of cover costs and power monotonicity (BG004) yield F002. S003 integrates only Borel constant indicators, with the countable integral interchange supplied directly by M001. The interval measure bound, nonnegative power identity and dyadic bound give c≤∑ρ_i^(s+1)+ε; BG005-BG013 check the routine omitted steps. Finite-partial-sum inequalities remain valid for infinite cover cost, and zero diameters contribute zero since s>0. In S004 c and V,ρ are independent of ε, so the positive-difference argument removes ε; S005 takes the infimum over all covers in the correct direction. No compactness, measurability of the arbitrary covering sets, signed convergence, or unproved limit exchange is used; n=0 and empty covering members cause no exception.

Every explicit input has an actual role: N001 gives c<∞ for positive s,δ; M002 integrates the pointwise bound; M001 interchanges the nonnegative countable sum and integral; M003 evaluates both sorts of constant indicators; M005 normalizes λ([0,1]); M006 evaluates the enlarging open intervals. Only the scale-content finiteness clause of N001 is used; its boundedness and dimension clauses need not be used. Fourteen recorded background notes account positively for routine real endpoint/diameter facts, square-root and real-power facts, basic indicator measurability and measure monotonicity, dyadic summation and finite-supremum bookkeeping. These do not replace the explicit core covering/integration proof or add hypotheses. The packet's calculation descriptions are not treated as permission to import measure theory or substantive theorems.
